title: Green Chile Chicken Stew
seoTitle: Green Chile Chicken Stew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Tomatillo and green chile stew with white beans for ten
subtitle: Tomatillo and green chile stew with white beans for ten
description: Chicken thighs braise with tomatillos, green chiles, and white beans until tender and tangy. Cumin and cilantro finish the pot for a bright, warming stew that is not standard chili.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Green Chile Chicken Stew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Char the tomatillos
steps.instruction: Broil tomatillos and onion at 500°F 5–7 minutes until blistered. Blend with green chiles and half the garlic until smooth. Target oven/smoker temperature: 500°F.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.instruction: Season chicken thighs and sear in oil 4 minutes per side until golden. Set aside. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer the stew
steps.instruction: Sauté remaining garlic and cumin 1 minute. Add tomatillo puree and broth. Return chicken and simmer 30 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Shred and finish
steps.instruction: Remove chicken, shred meat, discard bones. Return meat to pot with beans and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in half the cilantro. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Green Chile Chicken Stew onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Serve with garnishes
steps.instruction: Ladle into bowls and top with remaining cilantro and lime wedges. Offer hot sauce at the line. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Roasted poblano peppers diced in add smoky depth beyond canned chiles.
Corn kernels stirred in at the end make this feel like a complete bowl.
This thickens overnight—thin reheats with broth, not water.
tonightSpread: Stew with warm flour tortillas for dunking.
Shredded Monterey Jack and sour cream at the line.
leftovers: Layer over rice with fried egg for a green chile bowl breakfast.
Use as enchilada filling with extra cheese and sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Green chile stew feels different from the usual tomato chili rotation. It is hearty, tangy, and the heat level is easy to control for mixed spice tolerances on the crew.
mealPrepNotes: Roast fresh tomatillos under broiler for depth if using raw. Canned green chiles work fine for speed. Shred chicken in the pot after braising.
